messages:
Mia: Heads up — after HF->Redwood conversion for the new reranker model we onboarded, embeddings similarity is off. quick sanity: local HF embed vs Redwood-serving embed on the same weights disagree.
Sam: How big is the gap? random seed noise or systematic?
Mia: Systematic. On NQ eval, MRR dropped from 0.842 -> 0.798 when serving via Redwood runtime vs local HF inference. Not tiny.
Mia: Suspect tokenization/pooling mismatch. HF used a chat template that injects special system tokens and we might be accidentally including CLS tokens differently.
Anya: Can you paste the tokenizer/config differences?
Mia: Sure. HF config.json had these relevant bits:
```json
"model_type": "bert-like",
"add_prefix_space": false,
"bos_token": "<s>",
"eos_token": "</s>",
"cls_token": "<cls>",
"pad_token": "<pad>",
"truncation_strategy": "only_first"
```
Redwood conversion script generated: 
```json
"truncation_strategy": "longest_first",
"special_tokens_map": {"cls_token":"<s>"}
```
Mia: note the CLS remap and truncation change.
Oliver: That CLS remap is suspicious — mapping CLS to <s> will shift pooling index if we rely on token index 0. Also fastest_tokenizers (use_fast=True) can produce different offsets when special tokens are added.
Joon: Also check whether HF used `return_token_type_ids=False` in embed pipeline. Some batches assume pair-wise truncation. Truncation_strategy change can reorder which side gets trimmed.
Sam: Is the reranker using CLS pooling (embedding = hidden[state_index_of_cls]) or mean pooling ignoring pads?
Mia: Reranker expected CLS pooling (we index first occurrence of cls token). HF runs produced CLS at token idx 1 (because of a leading <s>), but Redwood-serving version has leading pad or different special token order — so our index lookup was off but still returned a vector (some other token) -> semantic mismatch.
Anya: So two bugs: 1) conversion remapped special tokens, 2) truncation strategy changed. Both explain systematic drop.
Mia: Repro steps I ran: 
```bash
# local HF
python eval/embeddings_eval.py --model hf/mymodel --tokenizer hf/mymodel --pooling cls --truncation only_first
# served Redwood (client)
python eval/embeddings_eval.py --model redwood://mymodel --pooling cls
```
Mia: HF local MRR 0.842, Redwood client 0.798. Token counts for a failing query: HF tokens [<s>, <cls>, ...], Redwood tokens [<pad>, <s>, <cls>, ...] — off by one.
Sam: Quick mitigation: change pooling code to find cls token by token id (tokenizer.cls_token_id) instead of assuming fixed index. That buys us safety across templates.
Oliver: Agreed. Also enforce explicit truncation config in conversion: set `truncation_strategy` to the tokenizer's original and preserve `add_special_tokens` ordering.
Mia: I pushed a quick script to detect these mismatches and fail conversion if special token ordering differs. @ci-bot triggered tests — but we should add a unit test that compares tokenized->offsets between hf and converted tokenizer for a few templates.
ci-bot: CI: conversion-checks passed on main for 3 commits.
ci-bot: Added integration test `test_tokenizer_equivalence.py` (runs on small sample).
Anya: Also noticed quantized runtime had slightly different behavior with KV-cache and padding; when quantized the runtime was left-padding sequences for perf which changed positions. We should make padding_side explicit in config (left vs right).
Mia: Good catch. HF template used `padding_side="right"`. Redwood default for that model was left. That explains the shift in many cases.
Joon: For action items I'd propose:
- immediate: change pooling lookup to `tokenizer.cls_token_id` and fall back to searching tokens. (Sam)
- conversion: preserve `truncation_strategy`, `padding_side`, and mapping of `cls_token` exactly. (Oliver)
- tests: add tokenization equivalence tests + a small end-to-end embedding MRR smoke test comparing 100 queries. (Anya / Mia)
- longer: run quantization experiments with explicit pad/trunc settings to confirm no regression. (Joon)

Sam: I'll open a PR with the pooling safety change now.
Mia: Thanks. Also logging note: add `token_ids_snapshot` to eval logs so we can quickly diff token sequences between HF and rw.
Oliver: I'll update conversion tool to copy `tokenizer.json` as-is and add a `conversion_metadata.json` with the original tokenizer attrs we must preserve. That should reduce surprises.
Mia: TL;DR — mismatch from special token remap + padding_side + truncation_strategy. Fix pooling lookup, preserve tokenizer attrs during conversion, add tests. :thumbsup:
Sam: On it.
Mia: I'll rerun the NQ eval after the pooling fix and report numbers in this thread.
Mia: quick status update — re-run after pooling fix: MRR back to 0.839 (small diff probably due to randomness). Looks much better.
Mia: leaving final verification tickets for quantization-run and conversion-tooling.
Oliver: Nice. Closing loop once quantized runs are green.
Mia: Thanks everyone.
